mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where CPI YoY > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in one month signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes an economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where UNRATE increases by more than 0.5pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals a weakening consumer demand, which leads to reduced corporate revenues and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where RSAFS declines for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to increased economic activity and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increases by more than 1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is above 2% year-over-year, the combination signals a potential overheating economy with loose monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: loose monetary policy with inflationary pressure
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL YoY > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to increased consumer spending and corporate revenues, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where PAYEMS increases for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When Housing Starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% year-over-year and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises by more than 0.5 percentage points in one month, the combination signals a weakening demand and labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST YoY decline > 10% and UNRATE increases > 0.5pp
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where HOUST declines by more than 10% YoY and UNRATE increases by more than 0.5pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to increased corporate profits and investor confidence, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where GDPC1 increases for two consecutive quarters.
